topic: Correcting unequal shares called halves or fourths

traps.desc: shared the strip into four parts instead of two

problems.desc: Part (c): the child says why the two parts of the strip are not halves. Full credit for the idea that halves must be the same size and part A covers more squares than part B, so cutting the strip anywhere except the middle does not make halves. Accept a count said aloud (five squares against three) or a matching argument (the parts do not line up when laid on top of each other). Half credit for saying only that the parts look different, with no reference to the squares. No credit for an answer that only names which part is bigger, since part (a) already asks for that.

traps.desc: shared the strip into two parts instead of four

problems.desc: Part (c): the child says why the four parts are not fourths. Full credit for the idea that fourths must all be the same size, and here the parts hold different numbers of squares, so cutting a strip into four pieces is not enough -- the four pieces have to match. Accept a count of any two parts that differ. Half credit for saying only that there are four parts so it must be fourths, corrected on the spot with help. No credit for naming the biggest part alone, since part (a) already asks for that.

traps.desc: shared the strip into four parts instead of two
shared the strip into two parts instead of four

problems.desc: Part (c): the child says which parts must change and how. Full credit for naming part A as too big and parts C and D as too small, and for saying every part has to end up with the same number of squares as the others. Accept a description of moving the cuts so that each piece covers three squares. Half credit for naming only one part that is wrong. No credit for an answer that only repeats the count of a true fourth, since part (b) already asks for that.

traps.desc: shared the rectangle into four parts instead of two

problems.desc: Part (c): the child explains why two parts of different shapes can still fail to be halves, and how to fix this rectangle. Full credit for the idea that halves are about the amount covered, not the shape of the piece, and that part A covers more squares than part B here, so the cut must move until each part covers the same number. Accept a described fix such as cutting straight down the middle of the rectangle instead. Half credit for saying only that the pieces are different shapes. No credit for an answer that only names the bigger part, since part (a) already asks for that.

Part (c): the child says whether Ella is right that cutting more pieces makes each piece bigger. Full credit for saying she is wrong, with the reason that the same strip is being shared among more parts, so each part gets less -- a fourth of the strip covers three squares while a half covers six. Accept the idea shown by the two strips rather than said in words. Half credit for saying she is wrong with no reason. No credit for agreeing with her.
